messages:
Ibrahim T.: hi all, onboarding week. following k8s quickstart but `kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox` returns Forbidden. set context to redwood-dev-eu per doc. any quick fixes?

Onboarding Bot: welcome! make sure SSO + kubeconfig sync are done: `redwoodctl login --sso` then `redwoodctl sync-kubeconfig`. link: https://intranet.redwood/dev-onboarding#k8s.

Ibrahim T.: I did SSO. current-context shows redwood-dev-eu but output:
```
kubectl config current-context
# redwood-dev-eu
kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox
# Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "system:anonymous" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "dev-sandbox"
```

Claire P.: that anonymous error = missing creds. common cause: KUBECONFIG points to multiple files and one file lacks user token. run `echo $KUBECONFIG` and `kubectl config view --minify --raw` (mask tokens) to check.

Ibrahim T.: `echo $KUBECONFIG` -> `/home/ibrahim/.kube/config:/home/ibrahim/.kube/old` (I forgot an old file).

Alex H.: yep. either unset KUBECONFIG or point it to the synced single config. try:
```
unset KUBECONFIG
redwoodctl sync-kubeconfig --cluster=redwood-dev-eu
kubectl config use-context redwood-dev-eu
kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox
```

Ibrahim T.: ran those. `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` -> "no". filed INFRA-9944 per infra-bot.

infra-bot: INFRA-9944 created: new-hire RBAC check for ibrahimt. Current: not in group "redwood:devs". Please add GitHub handle to the ticket for automatic binding.

Ibrahim T.: added GH handle. small question: how do I avoid accidentally hitting prod? I had prod contexts in my old file.

Claire P.: good catch. move prod contexts to a separate kubeconfig and do not merge during onboarding. we recommend `kubectl config rename-context` and `kubectl config unset users.<user>-prod` if needed. also set namespace default: `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=dev-sandbox`.

infra-bot: INFRA-9944 updated: applied rolebinding `namespace=dev-sandbox role=edit subject=group:redwood:devs`. Sync job completed.

Ibrahim T.: ~12m later: `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n dev-sandbox` -> "yes" and `kubectl get pods -n dev-sandbox` shows pods. resolved, thanks!

Alex H.: welcome! quick tips: 1) test perms with `kubectl auth can-i` before running anything destructive, 2) avoid `kubectl delete` without `--namespace`, 3) prefer `--dry-run=client` when experimenting. ping me if you want a 15m namespace tour.

Ibrahim T.: thanks all, adding notes to my onboarding checklist and the doc suggestion re: KUBECONFIG merging and prod-safety. :thumbsup:
